test_title: PYST 38: SSC CGL 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 24th_September_2025_Shift_2)
subject: maths
question: A wholesaler marks up a batch of 100 identical clocks by 80% on cost and offers a trade discount of 25% to retailers. A retailer purchases all the clocks and spends Rs. 48,000. What is the cost price per clock for the wholesaler?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net profit % = 80 − 25 − (80 × 25) ÷ 100 = 35%

Selling Price (SP) of 1 clock = 48000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 480

Cost Price (CP) × 1.35 = 480 ⇒ CP = 480 ÷ 1.35

CP = 3200 ÷ 9 ≈ Rs. 355.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 355.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total clocks = 100

Total amount paid by retailer = Rs. 48,000

Markup % = 80%

Discount % = 25%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (1 + Markup%/100) × (1 − Discount%/100)

 
 
 
 CP = ? SP = 480 MP 
 Markup: +80% 
 Discount: −25% 
 Net: +35% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP of 1 clock = 48000 ÷ 100 = Rs. 480

⇒ 480 = CP × (1 + 80/100) × (1 − 25/100)

⇒ 480 = CP × 1.80 × 0.75

⇒ 480 = CP × 1.35

⇒ CP = 480 ÷ 1.35

⇒ CP = 48000 ÷ 135

⇒ CP = 3200 ÷ 9 ≈ 355.56

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 355.56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Final Selling Price = MP × (1 − Discount%/100).

Effective Profit %

When a markup% and a discount% are applied, Effective profit % = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given successively, the equivalent net discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.
